note: City of Lakeway, Texas — Code of Ordinances, Chapter 30 Zoning, Article 30.03 "Zoning Use Regulations" (§ 30.03.001 – § 30.03.023), which defines one base district per numbered section and carries that district's "Minimum building setbacks" block. This is a classic enumerated Euclidean ordinance (each district has its own numbered section), not a form-based code, so the front/side/rear numbers are direct district-specific citations. ROUTE: read from the eCode360 article page at the citation_url above, whose copy of Article 30.03 DOES render the full section text and the flattened setback blocks to a plain fetch (verified 2026-09-16; unlike Chapter 3 of Jonestown's UDC, no print endpoint was needed for this article). The setback blocks are FLATTENED TABLES: each cell is rendered on its own line ("Street(s):" / "25" / "Side:" / "5 (golf course 25)"), so the quotes below render each block as its label/value sequence with the cell text unaltered. No number is paraphrased, rounded or converted. VINTAGE (checked at source before extracting): each section cited here carries its own trailing amendment line, and the most recent amending ordinance named anywhere in the article is Ordinance 2026-06-15-02 adopted 6/15/2026, which appears in the amendment line attached to § 30.03.009 (C-1); Ordinance 2025-06-16-02 adopted 6/16/2025 appears in the amendment line attached to § 30.03.023 (VPCO). No section in the article carries an amendment newer than 6/15/2026, so the dimensional text read here is in force and is not a retired scheme. The ordinance is in force; nothing here is a retired scheme. The City's zoning layer is already staged for this jurisdiction (8,202 of 8,259 census parcels carry a district stamp), so this table's job is to fill an existing router gap, not to create a zoning source. SENTINEL CONVENTION: every not_specified field carries the numeric sentinel 999 together with provenance.not_specified = true and a verbatim quote of the source language that caused the gap. 999 sits outside every gate sanity band, so if a not_specified flag were ever dropped the value would FLAG rather than silently read as a real standard. CONDITIONAL (NON-SCALAR) CELLS. Where the source states a base value plus a conditional exception — the recurring "(golf course 25)" parenthetical on the R-district side and rear yards, R-2's "(10' if adjacent to external residential)", R-8's "(25 ft. if abutting R-4, R-5, R-6, or R-7 districts)", and the "10*" / "*A minimum of 10 feet except a minimum of 40 feet for any side(s) that adjoin residential usage ... or golf course" pattern in HM, GUI, AV and REC — the GENERAL/BASE value is codified and the conditional exception is preserved verbatim in that field's provenance quote, matching the precedent set by hutto-tx.json and belton-tx.json. The conditional branch is NOT dropped and must not be read as absent. TIERED SETBACKS (C-1, C-2, C-3): these three districts state their setbacks twice over, keyed first on whether the building abuts a residential or a nonresidential use and then on building footprint ("0–50,000 sq. ft." vs "50,000 and greater" / "50,000 - 100,000 sq. ft."). Four combinations are therefore in force per district and no single number is the district's setback. The base case codified here is the SMALLEST-FOOTPRINT, NONRESIDENTIAL-ABUTTING column ("0–50,000 sq. ft." under "when abutting a nonresidential usage"), which appears in every one of the three sections, and the full four-combination block is quoted verbatim in each affected field's provenance. A caller must not read the codified figure as the setback for a 50,000+ sq. ft. building or for a building abutting a residence. OMITTED (deliberate): § 30.03.020 GB (Greenbelts) carries no dimensional block in the article; § 30.03.021 PUD is expressly a negotiated district whose standards "are described in the adopting ordinance for that district" and § 30.03.021(g)(2) lists the dimensional topics the PUD application must itself define, which is the PUD-refusal case rather than a table row; § 30.03.023 VPCO (View Protection Conditional Overlay) is an overlay that "do[es] not negate any of the base zoning district regulations except for maximum height", and that height is set case by case by the ZAPCO up to the base district's 32 ft., so it cannot be reduced to a district row. NOT READ: Articles 30.02 (establishment of districts/map), 30.04 and following were not read this pass, and Article 28.10 (environmental and impervious cover) — which several districts' lot-coverage lines point at — was not read, so every lot-coverage and impervious-cover figure that the source does not state numerically is coded 999/not_specified rather than estimated from that article. No cross-check against a second primary source was possible: this jurisdiction has no code-section atom corpus, so every value is primary-source-verified.
